decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm approach to left basket, lifting and gradually pitching the open gripper down while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Advance over the basket toward its far-right egg, continuing the gradual downward orientation with clearance.
Bring the left gripper nearly vertical above the far-right egg, keeping the fingers open and approaching gradually.
Fine approach to the far egg: lower the open fingers while shifting slightly forward and left to align at egg height.
Close around the aligned egg, then make a short vertical lift to check retention visually before transferring.
The egg is visible between the fingers. Lift clear of the rim and carry it toward the holder with the left gripper closed.
Carry the retained egg above the holder's left rear cup and start lowering; final centering will be checked from RGB.
Tracking lag and proximity to the upright lid are visible. Replan slowly from the actual pose, moving toward the front of the cup before lowering.
Retry with smaller increments toward the prior direction while easing away from the lid; no movement occurred in the rejected chunk.
The egg has slipped beside the holder. Open and retreat upward and toward the robot to clear the lid before recovering it.
Reorient above the holder to approach the slipped egg from the left with jaws parallel to the lid edge, reducing collision risk.
Finish turning the jaws along the lid edge while approaching the loose egg from above-left.
Lower the open gripper beside the hinge toward the loose egg, keeping the palm outside the holder.
Tracking suggests contact with the lid. Move left away from it and make the approach more vertical before descending again.
Approach the visible loose egg from outside the lid, tilting the fingers inward while keeping the wrist farther left.
Make a short inward/downward adjustment toward the loose egg and start closing only after the approach.
Seat the fingers slightly lower around the loose egg, close, then test with a small lift.
Lift the recovered egg safely in the left gripper. The lid has fallen closed, so begin positioning the right arm to reopen it.
The loose egg remained on the table. Keep the left arm clear and bring the right open gripper above the lid's front edge for reopening.
Reduce right-arm increments after the continuity rejection. With the lid flat, align the left fingers over the loose egg.
Close the left fingers around the loose egg after a short fine descent. Bring the right gripper toward the lid's front-right edge.
Seat the left grasp slightly deeper and test a small lift. Finish angling the right fingers toward the lid's front edge.
The loose egg rolled behind the holder, so clear the left hand. Lower and close the right gripper on the front lid edge to reopen it.
Close fully at the lid lip and test a gradual lifting arc with the right hand; keep the left arm stationary and clear.
The lid did not lift. Reopen the right fingers and descend closer to its front lip rather than pulling from above it.
Close at the contacted lid edge and test a small upward-and-back motion, checking whether the lid follows.
The front edge appears slightly lifted. Continue the opening arc while keeping the right fingers closed and the left arm clear.
The lid is visibly opening. Follow its hinge arc with the right hand to raise it farther without dragging the holder.
The lid slipped closed. Return the right hand to the front edge for a lower grip, while positioning the left hand over the loose egg behind the holder.
Retry the right retreat at smaller increments after the zero-step rejection; left remains in its workspace approaching the loose egg.
Fine-center and close around the loose egg. Return the right gripper to the front lip with an open aperture for a renewed lid grasp.
The left fingers are still shallow on the egg. Open and seat them lower, then close and test a short lift; regrasp the lid lip with the right.
Correct the left grasp laterally using the wrist view and seat farther over the egg. Lift the lid again with the right hand, keeping it grasped.
Recenter the left fingertips rather than pressing down against the table. Reposition the right jaw farther outside the front lip and lower for an under-edge grasp.
Shift the left grasp laterally to center the egg between both jaws. Close the right fingers on the front lip and lift mainly upward before sweeping back.
Clear and steepen the left approach to avoid the holder. Reset the right fingers to the lip orientation that previously lifted the lid.
Regrasp the lid at the previously effective depth and raise its front edge, leaving the left hand clear.
Follow the lid's hinge with both wrist translation and rotation, maintaining the right grasp. Move the left hand out of the opening arc.
The lid is now visibly raised. Continue the hinge-centered opening arc with the right gripper closed.
Continue opening in smaller hinge-following increments as the right arm becomes more folded, keeping the lid grasped.
The lid is open but further rotation reaches the right arm's limit. Hold it steady there and use the left arm to retrieve a basket egg from above.
Descend vertically onto the basket's near-right egg with open fingers; keep the reopened lid undisturbed.
Center the near-right egg between the left jaws, descend the last few centimeters, close, and test retention with a short lift.
The egg is visibly enclosed by the left fingers. Lift above the basket and start transferring toward the front-left cup, keeping the lid open.
Carry the egg vertically above the holder's front-left opening, away from the raised lid, then begin a controlled descent.
Tracking indicates contact near the raised lid/right hand. Route the retained egg toward the front of the holder before continuing inward.
Lower toward the front-left cup with a slight inward finger tilt, keeping the wrist outside the right hand's space.
The egg is immediately above the front-left opening. Make a small centering correction, release, and withdraw to inspect placement.
Keep the left fingers open and withdraw toward the front-left to clear contact and let the egg settle.
An egg is now visible resting in the holder. Return the open left hand toward the basket while keeping clearance from the holder and right arm.
Approach the nearer of the two remaining basket eggs with vertical, open left fingers. Keep the right hand stationary at the lid.
The nearer basket egg is centered between the open fingers. Descend, close, and make a short retention-check lift.
Both basket eggs entered the wide grasp. Open, lift slightly, and shift toward the nearer egg to isolate it before closing again.
The eggs separated after reopening. Recenter on the nearer egg's new position, close on that egg alone, and test a short lift.
Lift the isolated basket egg and carry it around the front of the holder, avoiding the stationary right hand and raised lid.
Move the retained egg above the empty front-left cup using a front approach, with the wrist kept left of center.
Use the wrist view to bring the held egg inward and forward over the empty front-left opening, descending gradually.
The egg is near the cup's front rim. Lift slightly while fine-centering it over the opening rather than pressing against the rim.
Fine-center the egg above the empty left cup, lower gently, and open the fingers to let it settle.
Withdraw the open left fingers upward and left so the released egg can settle, then inspect the holder.
Two eggs are visible in the holder. Return the open left hand to the remaining basket egg while maintaining lid clearance.
Approach the last basket egg with the open left fingers, then inspect its alignment before descending to grasp.
The last basket egg shifted toward the far side. Fine-center the open left jaws on its current position and descend gradually.
The last basket egg is centered. Seat the left jaws slightly lower, close, and lift to verify retention.
Lift the retained last basket egg and carry it around the front toward an empty holder cup, with the lid kept open.
Carry the third egg toward the empty front-left cup, keeping a front approach and checking the wrist view before release.
Fine-center over the empty left-front opening and lower while maintaining the grasp; use the next wrist view to judge rim clearance.
The held egg is still outside the left rim. Lift slightly and angle the fingers inward over the empty cup without moving the left wrist across center.
Angle the held egg a little farther inward over the empty front cup, lower gently, and begin opening once centered.
Fully open and withdraw the left fingers upward and left to inspect the third egg's seating without disturbing the lid.
Three eggs are visibly seated. Clear the holder and look toward the remaining loose egg behind the lid with the left wrist camera.
Move the left camera around the left side of the raised lid to locate the loose fourth egg, keeping both hands separated.
The loose egg is partially visible behind the lid. Approach from its left-rear side, tilting the open fingers inward while keeping the wrist left of center.
Contact is blocking the side approach. Retreat left and behind the lid while rotating the jaw opening direction to avoid straddling the lid edge.
